# Notio

> Notio (codename) is a pure-Rust FHIR terminology server for SNOMED CT, LOINC, and other clinical code systems, SNOMED CT first. It serves the HL7 FHIR terminology API (`$lookup`, `$subsumes`, `$validate-code`, `$expand`, `$translate`) across R4, R4B, R5, and R6 from one running server, backed by a memory-mapped, index-materialized concept store, with no JVM and no Elasticsearch. The FHIR layer is generated from the vendored machine-readable FHIR packages; the engine (a code-system-neutral store, hierarchy, and search substrate, with per-system loaders such as SNOMED RF2 and ECL evaluation) is hand-written. Notio ships no AI: no model is trained, embedded, or called at request time. AI coding assistance is used to build it, under human review.

## Start here

- [README](README.md): what Notio is, why it exists, and the architecture in brief.
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): the design authority, with the five defining decisions and their citations.
- [Code systems](docs/terminologies.md): the catalogue of code systems Notio serves or plans to serve (identity, distribution, licence, hierarchy, FHIR-defined filters) and the build order, SNOMED CT first.
- [Working discipline](CLAUDE.md): the engineering rules for changing the code, and the repo map.

## Design and scope

- [Implementation checklist](docs/implementation.md): what the server must do; the project has no fixed version scope, so release contents are decided during development.
- [Version matrix](docs/VERSIONS.md): the pinned FHIR, SNOMED, Rust, and dependency versions.
- [CI/CD and supply chain](docs/ci-cd.md): the SLSA Build Level 3 release lane, signed SBOMs, and the security workflows.

## Rules (`.claude/rules/`)

- [spec-adherence.md](.claude/rules/spec-adherence.md): the FHIR and SNOMED CT / ECL specifications are the oracle; strictness and citation.
- [fhir-terminology.md](.claude/rules/fhir-terminology.md): FHIR wire conformance for the terminology operations, versioning, and paging.
- [snomed-terminology.md](.claude/rules/snomed-terminology.md): the SNOMED URI standard, implicit value sets and concept maps, ECL, and RF2 handling.
- [codegen.md](.claude/rules/codegen.md): the generated `notio-fhir` layer; never hand-edit a `// @generated` file.
- [testing.md](.claude/rules/testing.md): test discipline, and the acceptance oracles (the HL7 `fhir-tx-ecosystem-ig` cases, and differential testing against Snowstorm and Hermes).
- [reliability.md](.claude/rules/reliability.md): the machine-enforced safety rules (no `unsafe`, typed errors, deny-tier lints).
- [rust-style.md](.claude/rules/rust-style.md): idiomatic Rust style and import discipline.
- [comments.md](.claude/rules/comments.md): comment budgets (RFC 505 and RFC 1574).
- [writing-style.md](.claude/rules/writing-style.md): the prose rules for all human-facing text (no AI tells).
- [ai-code-review.md](.claude/rules/ai-code-review.md): SonarQube Cloud is an advisory second opinion, never authority.
- [vendored-inputs.md](.claude/rules/vendored-inputs.md): vendored FHIR packages are codegen input; SNOMED CT content is never committed.
- [issue-workflow.md](.claude/rules/issue-workflow.md): the GitHub Issues work loop.
